# When the original post used what scene construction method in general simulation, RGB-only humanoid robot strategy is difficult to sim-to-real?

> **Current answer:** The candidate process involves scanning the real deployment site using the same reconstruction to generate 3D Gaussian Splat and collision mesh, and training and incorporating domain randomization (DR) and a large visual encoder in Isaac Sim/Lab. This aims to align visual and physical geometry. Since no independent experiments were provided, this remains a pending verification scheme.

## Key terms

- Whole-Body Control (WBC) (全身控制)
- Simulation-to-Real (Sim2Real), Sim-to-Real (仿真到现实)
- Domain Randomization (DR) (域随机化)

## Problem and symptoms

- RGB strategies in general-purpose random geometry and no-texture simulations are difficult to generalize to real deployment sites.
- General pseudo-scenarios teach structure only, and cannot cover real materials, lighting, or semantics; real machine collision could cause hardware damage and long reinitializations.

## Environment

- Real office 360° scan; measurement scale Gaussian Splat; shared collision mesh; Isaac Sim/Lab; RGB-only navigation strategy.

## Priority diagnostics

- Verify that the visual reconstruction and collision mesh come from the same scene and scale; record friction, mass, ground softness, and site changes.

## Possible causes

- Visual appearance and physical collision geometry are inconsistent; domain randomization does not cover debris, friction, mass, or ground softness; site changes make the previous scan outdated.

## Attempts

- Perform a 360° scan to generate Gaussian Splat and collision mesh, and train an RGB strategy in the same scene.

## Effective fixes

- The original post's candidate scheme was on-site reconstruction plus a shared collision mesh, combined with domain randomization and a large visual encoder.

## Result

- The author claims no on-site tuning is needed for deployment, and site adaptation was reduced from several months to days; the original post lacks quantitative validation.

## Limitations

- No disclosure of robot, task success rate, randomization parameters, failure cases, or independent replication; the response indicated that debris, ground softness, and scan frequency remain boundaries.

## Safety notes

- Before deploying in real sites, validate the collision mesh, depth occlusion, glass doors, and ground compliance in low-speed, limited-force, and collision-avoidance conditions.

## Image and visual evidence

- A visible screenshot shows the first half of the original text, confirming its generalization of random, no-texture scenarios to real office reconstruction; the screenshot lacks logs, physical parameters, or success rate curves, so it cannot verify the 'zero on-site tuning' conclusion.

## Applicability boundary

- Suitable for deployment sites that can be pre-scanned and tasks with primary RGB perception; not suitable for dynamic or large open environments.
